segments.text: But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry.
And he prayed unto the LORD, and said,

segments.speaker: Jonah
segments.text: I pray thee, O LORD, was not this my saying, when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil.

segments.speaker: Jonah
segments.text: Therefore now, O LORD, take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live.

segments.speaker: the Lord
segments.text: Doest thou well to be angry?

footnotes.text: + Doest…: or, Art thou greatly angry?

segments.text: So Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made him a booth, and sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would become of the city.
And the LORD God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shadow over his head, to deliver him from his grief. So Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd.

footnotes.text: + was…: Heb. rejoiced with great joy

segments.text: But God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd that it withered.
And it came to pass, when the sun did arise, that God prepared a vehement east wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted, and wished in himself to die, and said,

segments.speaker: Jonah
segments.text: It is better for me to die than to live.

segments.speaker: Jonah
segments.text: And God said to Jonah, Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd? And he said, I do well to be angry, even unto death.

footnotes.text: + Doest…: or, Art thou greatly angry?
+ I do well…: or, I am greatly angry

segments.speaker: the Lord
segments.text: Thou hast had pity on the gourd, for the which thou hast not laboured, neither madest it grow; which came up in a night, and perished in a night:

footnotes.text: + came…: Heb. was the son of the night

segments.speaker: The LORD
segments.text: And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
